articles.title: Ultrasound-guided percutaneous catheter drainage of deep neck space abscesses: outcomes and predictors of treatment failure.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Clinical evidence supporting ultrasound-guided percutaneous catheter drainage (US-PCD) as a first-line treatment for deep neck space abscesses (DNSAs) remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of US-PCD as initial management for DNSAs and to identify factors associated with treatment efficacy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included patients with DNSAs who underwent US-PCD as a first-line treatment at four tertiary hospitals in China between 2015 and 2022. All patients were hemodynamically stable and had a stable airway, with preprocedural contrast-enhanced CT/MRI confirming no extensive mediastinal involvement beyond the anterosuperior compartment. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify preprocedural predictors of US-PCD efficacy. RESULTS: US-PCD was performed in 117 patients. The procedure was technically accessible in 116 (98%) patients, among whom 12 (10%) had descending mediastinitis confined to the anterosuperior mediastinum. No procedure-related major complications occurred. Drainage success was achieved in 98 patients (84%). Among the 18 patients (16%) in whom US-PCD failed, three (3%) died and the remaining 15 (13%) required open surgical drainage. Multiple septations and leukocyte count were significant in univariate but not multivariable analysis. The only independent predictor of drainage failure was the presence of serious associated events-a composite variable including descending mediastinitis, sepsis, airway compromise, and vascular thrombosis (OR = 5.7, 95% CI: 1.9-17.4, p = 0.002). CONCLUSION: Ultrasound-guided percutaneous catheter drainage represents an effective minimally invasive first-line option for selected patients with deep neck space abscesses; however, open surgery should be prioritized when serious associated events are present. KEY POINTS: Question For deep neck space abscesses (DNSAs), ultrasound-guided percutaneous drainage (US-PCD) is a common surgical alternative, but its outcomes and predictors as a first-line treatment remain unclear. Findings US-PCD was effective as a first-line treatment for selected DNSAs. Only serious associated events-mediastinitis, sepsis, airway compromise, and thrombosis-independently predicted drainage failure. Clinical relevance US-PCD may be considered a first-line minimally invasive option for hemodynamically and airway-stable DNSA patients, even with anterosuperior mediastinal extension. Surgical drainage remains prioritized for cases with serious associated events to achieve rapid infection control.

articles.title: Performance uncertainty in medical image analysis: A large-scale investigation of confidence intervals.
articles.abstract: Performance uncertainty quantification is essential for reliable validation and eventual clinical translation of medical imaging artificial intelligence (AI). Confidence intervals (CIs) play a central role in this process by indicating how precise a reported performance estimate is. Yet, due to the limited amount of work examining CI behavior in medical imaging, the community remains largely unaware of how many diverse CI methods exist and how they behave in specific settings. The purpose of this study is to close this gap. To this end, we conducted a large-scale empirical analysis across a total of 24 segmentation and classification tasks, using 19 trained models per task group, a broad spectrum of commonly used performance metrics, multiple aggregation strategies, and several widely adopted CI methods. Reliability (coverage) and precision (width) of each CI method were estimated across all settings to characterize their dependence on study characteristics. Our analysis revealed five principal findings: (1) the sample size required for reliable CIs varies from a few dozens to several thousands of cases depending on study parameters; (2) CI behavior is strongly affected by the choice of performance metric; (3) aggregation strategy substantially influences the reliability of CIs, e.g. they require more observations for macro than for micro; (4) the machine learning problem (segmentation versus classification) modulates these effects; (5) different CI methods are not equally reliable and precise depending on the use case. Finally, we derived practical implications of this study in the form of a decision tree which shall prove useful to the community. This paves the way for future consensus guidelines on reporting performance uncertainty.

articles.title: Noise2Match: Self-Supervised Low-Dose CT Denoising via Adaptive Inter-Slice Matching.
articles.abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning, supervised convolutional neural network methods have greatly improved the performance of low-dose computed tomography (CT) denoising. However, they require paired noisy-clean training data, which is difficult to obtain in practice. Some classic self-supervised denoising methods rely on the assumption of pixel-wise independent noise, making them ineffective for correlated noise in low-dose CT (LDCT) images. Considering the high similarity and weaker noise correlation between adjacent CT slices, several recently proposed self-supervised methods use adjacent LDCT slices for training. Nevertheless, these approaches fail to effectively account for the non-rigid mis-alignment between slices caused by anatomical variation, hindering them from satisfying the equal-mean condition required by the classic Noise2Noise framework. In this paper, we propose Noise2Match, a self-supervised LDCT denoising method based on adaptive inter-slice matching. Noise2Match introduces an inter-slice matching network to model the label transition process between adjacent slices, and then applies correction to the denoiser's outputs to better satisfy the equal-mean condition. We theoretically prove that, under idealized conditions, training Noise2Match using adjacent LDCT slices is equivalent to supervised training with paired noisy-clean images. We further find that Noise2Match can also effectively perform low-dose cone-beam CT (CBCT) denoising, which could be attributed to its correction operation that reduces inter-slice noise correlation. To the best of our knowledge, Noise2Match is the first effective image-domain self-supervised method for low-dose CBCT. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Noise2Match outperforms existing image-domain self-supervised methods, offering broader applicability and higher practical value.

articles.title: VERIDAH: solving enumeration anomaly-aware vertebra labeling across imaging sequences.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Although the identification of enumeration anomalies has potential clinical implications for chronic back pain and operation planning, the thoracolumbar junction is poorly assessed and rarely described in clinical reports. Additionally, even though multiple deep-learning-based vertebra labeling algorithms exist, there is a lack of methods to automatically label enumeration anomalies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We introduce "Vertebra Identification with Anomaly Handling" (VERIDAH), a novel vertebra labeling algorithm based on multiple classification heads combined with a weighted vertebra sequence prediction algorithm. We use the NAKO dataset for MRI and a CT cohort to retrospectively evaluate the labeling performance by computing how often the model is correct in predicting the vertebra labels, including enumeration anomalies. Statistical significance was assessed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. RESULTS: On 1000 T2w sagittal (mean age 52 ± 11, 52% female) and 365 CT (mean age 74 ± 21, 44% female) images, we show that our approach surpasses existing models on T2w TSE sagittal (98.30% vs. 94.24% of subjects with all vertebrae correctly labeled, p < 0.01) and CT imaging (99.18% vs. 77.26% of subjects with all vertebrae correctly labeled, p < 0.01) and works in arbitrary field-of-view images. VERIDAH correctly labeled the presence of thoracic enumeration anomalies in 87.80% and 96.30% of T2w and CT images, respectively, and lumbar enumeration anomalies in 94.48% and 97.22% for T2w and CT, respectively. CONCLUSION: VERIDAH offers enumeration anomaly robust vertebra labeling in CT and T2w sagittal imaging and is publicly released along with a spine segmentation model. KEY POINTS: QuestionAutomatically identifying enumeration anomalies in the spine is important in determining the correct vertebra labels, especially in limited field-of-view imaging. FindingsA carefully designed classifier with multiple classification heads and a sequence predictor provides superior results on large benchmarks, both in CT and MRI. Clinical relevanceThe proposed method identifies vertebra levels even in very limited field-of-view imaging, and correctly predicts enumeration anomalies, making downstream tasks such as surgery planning easier. Its public availability enables studies and applications to take these spinal anomalies into account.

articles.title: Multimodal Transformer Integrating CT and Pathology for Postoperative Risk Stratification in Stage I Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
articles.abstract: Purpose To develop and evaluate an interpretable, multimodal deep learning model to improve postoperative risk stratification and predict adjuvant therapy benefit in stage I non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Materials and Methods In this multicenter retrospective study of patients with stage I NSCLC, a multimodal model called the Deep Learning-Radiomic-Text Transformer (DLRTransformer) was developed by integrating multiview 2.5-dimensional deep learning features from CT scans, radiomics, clinical variables, and prognostic embeddings extracted from pathology reports using a large language model. A central transformer architecture fuses these features to predict disease-free survival. Model performance was evaluated on independent external datasets and compared with guideline-based risk stratification. Associations between model-derived risk scores and tumor microenvironment features were analyzed to assess biologic interpretability. Results A total of 1073 patients (mean age ± SD, 60.8 years ± 9.8; 550 male) were enrolled from five centers. On external datasets, DLRTransformer demonstrated robust prognostic performance (concordance index, 0.77-0.78), outperforming the guideline-based risk stratification (concordance index, 0.60-0.65). Risk scores were associated with tumor microenvironment phenotypes, including increased neoplastic cellularity and reduced tertiary lymphoid structures. A treatment-by-risk interaction was observed (interaction hazard ratio [HR], 0.14; 95% CI: 0.06, 0.32; P < .01). In propensity score-matched subcohorts, adjuvant therapy improved disease-free survival in high-risk patients (HR, 0.30; 95% CI: 0.11, 0.84; P = .02) but not in low-risk patients (HR, 1.70; 95% CI: 0.97, 2.99; P = .06). Conclusion The DLRTransformer improved postoperative risk stratification compared with guideline-based risk stratification and identified patients with stage I NSCLC who benefited from adjuvant therapy. Keywords: Deep Learning, Large Language Models LLMs, CT, Prognosis & Prediction, Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC), Multimodal Deep Learning, Risk Stratification, Adjuvant Therapy, Tumor Microenvironment (TME) Supplemental material is available for this article. © The Author(s) 2026. Published by the Radiological Society of North America under a CC BY 4.0 license.

articles.title: MRI and proton MR spectroscopy in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy: a comprehensive imaging review.
articles.abstract: Neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) remains a leading cause of neonatal mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental disability. Although cranial ultrasound is widely used as a bedside screening tool, brain MRI has become central to diagnosis, injury pattern classification, timing estimation, and outcome prediction. Furthermore, proton MR spectroscopy (1H-MRS) provides complementary metabolic biomarkers that enhance prognostication. This review focuses on MRI and 1H-MRS in neonatal encephalopathy due to hypoxic-ischemic injury, addressing both term and preterm infants. The pathophysiologic determinants of injury distribution are summarized, the optimal timing of imaging and diffusion evolution is discussed, and practical acquisition protocols including recommended sequences and 1H-MRS parameters are proposed. Key MRI phenotypes in term infants-basal ganglia-thalamus injury, watershed/parasagittal cortical-subcortical injury, and global or near-total injury patterns are reviewed with attention to common pitfalls such as diffusion pseudonormalization and evolving T1/T2 signal changes. For preterm infants, this review highlights distinctive vulnerabilities of the germinal matrix and periventricular white matter, emphasizing the spectrum from punctate white matter injury (WMI) to cystic periventricular leukomalacia (PVL). For 1H-MRS, voxel selection, echo time considerations, and interpretation of lactate, N-acetylaspartate (NAA), choline, creatine, and myo-inositol are detailed. Evidence suggests that deep gray matter lactate/NAA or NAA-based metrics serve as reliable and robust outcome biomarkers. Emerging directions including arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion are also discussed.

articles.title: A Survey of Computational Color Constancy: Approaches and Emerging Applications in Medical Imaging.
articles.abstract: As the evening sets in and natural light fades to artificial light, it is remarkable how the colors around us still appear nearly the same. This phenomenon, known as color constancy, allows us to perceive relatively stable colors even as lighting conditions change. In the field of computer vision, replicating this human ability is the key to performing tasks such as recognizing objects and understanding scenes. This review examines two main approaches to tackle the challenge of computational color constancy: traditional static methods that rely on a set of assumptions about lighting and scene conditions, and newer learning-based methods that use models trained to estimate lighting directly from images. We look at how these techniques have evolved, from foundational methods like the gray-world assumption, which work within certain limitations, to modern deep learning techniques that can interpret lighting in more dynamic ways. The datasets, metrics, and reported results of the surveyed studies are consolidated into two comparative tables, providing a structured overview of the methods discussed. Together, these comparisons offer a broad perspective on how computational color constancy has developed and where it is headed, with particular emphasis on its applications in medical imaging.

articles.title: Neurovascular coupling in simultaneous EEG-fNIRS studies: A scoping review of analytical frameworks and clinical applications.
articles.abstract: Simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) have been used across cognitive and physiological states and in diverse clinical populations. However, the interpretation of cross-modal coupling remains difficult because findings from different analytical frameworks, populations, and experimental conditions have not been systematically mapped. This scoping review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO, and IEEE Xplore were searched through February 10, 2026, for studies that quantitatively related simultaneously recorded EEG and fNIRS signals. Two reviewers independently screened the records. Findings were synthesized narratively, and analytical pipelines were mapped across the signal domain, feature extraction, coupling metric, and temporal lag handling. Fifty-seven studies were included. Amplitude-based studies related event-related potentials and oscillatory EEG features to focal hemodynamic responses, with associations varying across electrophysiological features, cortical regions, and task conditions. Frequency- and scale-specific analyses identified band-dependent relationships, while coupling at ultra-slow scales showed sensitivity to vascular and systemic physiological influences. Studies that explicitly modeled timing identified several-second offsets in some paradigms, while directional estimates varied across tasks and recording states. Network analyses showed partial and context-dependent correspondence between EEG- and fNIRS-derived measures, while model-based approaches characterized multivariate and predictive cross-modal relationships. Across frameworks, observed coupling differed with recording state, frequency band, cortical region, and temporal lag handling rather than representing a single quantity. Clinical findings were heterogeneous, and most condition-specific patterns were supported by small and methodologically diverse evidence bases. These findings support framework-matched analysis and pipeline-explicit reporting when interpreting EEG-fNIRS coupling.

articles.title: Neural dynamics of auditory attention: Interactions between top-down and bottom-up processes.
articles.abstract: Auditory attention allows listeners to navigate complex acoustic environments by prioritizing behaviorally-relevant sounds while limiting interference from competing input. This process is guided by a dynamic interplay between top-down attention, driven by behavioral goals and expectations, and bottom-up attention, triggered by stimulus-driven salience. Although this distinction remains useful at a conceptual level, growing evidence suggests that auditory attention emerges from continuous interactions between goal-directed and stimulus-driven processes that recruit partially overlapping neural systems and vary with task demands, stimulus properties, and prior experience. This review focuses on the neural mechanisms underlying attentional control and interactions between top-down and bottom-up auditory attention. It synthesizesevidence from neurophysiological, behavioral, and neuroimaging studies and explores how top-down control modulates the neural processing and attentional impact of salient input, how bottom-up signals override attentional focus, and how these interactions are shaped by task demands and individual cognitive capacity. The findings synthesized here support a view of auditory attention as a flexible and adaptive system, whose operation emerges from context-dependent interactions, with important implications for models of attention and real-world listening behaviors.

articles.title: Deep learning reconstruction in prostate MRI: technical principles, clinical applications, and future directions.
articles.abstract: Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) has become integral to the detection, localization, risk stratification, and management of prostate cancer. Increasing utilization of prostate MRI in screening, active surveillance, targeted biopsy guidance, and treatment planning has amplified the demand for faster imaging protocols while maintaining high diagnostic quality. Conventional MRI acceleration strategies, including parallel imaging and compressed sensing, improve acquisition efficiency but remain limited by trade-offs involving signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), image sharpness, artifacts, and reconstruction complexity. Deep learning reconstruction (DLR) has emerged as a promising artificial intelligence-based approach for MRI acceleration and image enhancement. Unlike traditional reconstruction methods that rely primarily on predefined mathematical models, DLR uses neural networks to learn image priors and reconstruction features from MRI data. Published studies suggest that DLR may enable accelerated acquisitions while maintaining or, in some settings, improving image quality through denoising, artifact reduction, and improved spatial resolution and lesion conspicuity. However, these effects vary according to the reconstruction algorithm, sequence, acceleration factor, and clinical setting. Variational networks combine physics-based MRI constraints with learned regularization and represent an important framework for DLR. In prostate MRI, available studies have reported substantial reductions in acquisition time for T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted imaging while generally maintaining perceived image quality. Reported benefits include improved lesion conspicuity, reader confidence, and delineation of anatomic structures. Current evidence suggests that DLR generally preserves PI-RADS assessment and diagnostic performance rather than systematically altering lesion categorization; however, evidence demonstrating improvements in diagnostic accuracy or clinical outcomes remains limited. Important limitations include vendor and algorithm dependence, potential reconstruction artifacts, variability in quantitative imaging metrics, limited multicenter validation, and uncertain generalizability across scanners, protocols, and clinical settings. This review summarizes the technical principles underlying DLR, discusses current clinical applications in prostate MRI, highlights representative studies and workflow implications, reviews limitations, and outlines future directions for this rapidly evolving technology.

articles.title: Letter to the Editor: Methodological and biophysical concerns on quantitative DCE-MRI for early PDAC response assessment.

Balloon-Occlusion Versus End-Hole Transarterial Chemoembolization for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of balloon-occluded transarterial chemoembolization (B-TACE) compared with conventional (cTACE) and drug-eluting-bead transarterial chemoembolization (DEB-TACE) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO. PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched to 8 February 2026 for randomized and observational studies comparing B-TACE with cTACE or DEB-TACE. Tumor response (mRECIST), overall survival, and adverse events were pooled using random-effects models; risk of bias was assessed with established tools. RESULTS: Nine studies (one randomized, eight observational; 1534 patients) were included. Complete response, objective response, disease control, and progressive disease did not differ significantly between groups, with moderate-to-substantial heterogeneity. Baseline tumors were larger in the balloon-occluded group (mean difference 4.34 mm; 95% CI 1.18- 7.50; p = 0.014). Exploratory study-level analyses suggested greater relative B-TACE effects with larger tumors, particularly for complete response and disease control.Overall survival favored B-TACE in the two studies with extractable hazard ratios (HR 0.41; 95% CI 0.23 to 0.73; p = 0.002). Post-treatment liver enzymes, bilirubin, fever, and post-embolization syndrome did not differ significantly. CONCLUSION: No statistically significant differences in imaging response or safety were observed between intervention and comparator groups, while B-TACE was associated with a signal toward improved overall survival despite larger baseline tumors. Exploratory findings suggested that larger tumor size may be associated with a greater relative B-TACE effect. Given the limited evidence, these findings require confirmation in randomized controlled trials.

articles.title: AI-enhanced routine CT for opportunistic osteoporosis screening and risk assessment.
articles.abstract: Osteoporosis-related fractures create a large and often preventable burden, yet many individuals undergoing CT for unrelated care do not receive skeletal assessment. This review evaluates artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled use of routine CT for opportunistic case-finding and risk assessment, with emphasis on the boundary between promising retrospective performance and safe clinical implementation. Automated vertebral segmentation and CT-derived bone-density estimation can reduce manual workload, and published diagnostic studies report high discrimination in selected cohorts. However, pooled estimates are heterogeneous because the reference standard, anatomical target, CT acquisition, reconstruction, contrast status, calibration method, prevalence, and validation design differ substantially across studies. These differences preclude a universal CT threshold or a universal minimum detector-row requirement; detector-row configuration should be considered together with the broader acquisition and reconstruction parameters. For implementation, AI should be deployed as a validated triage tool-not as a stand-alone diagnostic replacement for clinical assessment and indicated DXA/QCT. A credible pathway requires a defined CT-protocol eligibility check; pre-specified vertebral region of interest and exclusions; protocol- and contrast-aware quantification; scanner-specific quality assurance and calibration monitoring where applicable; external validation in representative populations; and an explicit route from an AI alert to confirmatory testing and treatment evaluation. AI may also enable concurrent vertebral-fracture and body-composition assessment, but clinical utility must be shown through downstream testing, treatment, fracture, workload, equity, and cost outcomes. The near-term priority is therefore not higher retrospective diagnostic performance alone, but reproducible, transparent, and prospectively evaluated integration into radiology workflows.

articles.title: Palliative radiotherapy for gastric cancer-related bleeding: a systematic review and meta-analysis of bleeding response and dose-response relationships.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Palliative radiotherapy is commonly used to control bleeding in advanced gastric cancer; however, the optimal dose-fractionation regimen as well as the dose-response relationship remain unclear. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of radiotherapy for gastric cancer-related bleeding and its association with dose fractionation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and Ichushi-Web for studies published between January 2000 and August 2026 on palliative radiotherapy for gastric cancer-related bleeding. The primary endpoint was bleeding response rate. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate the pooled response rates. Meta-regression and subgroup analyses were conducted to explore dose-response relationships. Meta-regression was performed using study-level median biologically effective dose (BED) values. RESULTS: A total of 31 studies were included. The pooled bleeding response rate was 75.9% (95% confidence interval, 69.7-81.2), with significant heterogeneity (I2 = 67.5%). Egger's test suggested small study effects (P = 0.012). Meta-regression analysis demonstrated an association between a higher BED and an increased likelihood of response (P = 0.010). Subgroup analyses showed that higher BED categories were associated with higher response rates (P = 0.005). The pooled rebleeding rate was 32.4%. The median overall survival and rebleeding-free survival were 3.8 and 3.4 months, respectively. Radiotherapy was generally well tolerated, with a low incidence of grade ≥ 3 toxicities. CONCLUSIONS: Palliative radiotherapy is an effective and well-tolerated treatment for gastric cancer-related bleeding. Although study-level meta-regression identified a statistical association between higher BED and hemostatic response, this may largely reflect selection bias and methodological limitations rather than a true dose-response relationship. Given the poor prognosis of this population, shorter dose-fractionation regimens are appropriate for many patients, whereas higher-BED regimens remain reasonable for selected patients.

articles.title: MRI-defined parametrial venous invasion in locally advanced cervical cancer: association with pathological venous invasion, pretreatment lymph node metastasis, and survival outcomes.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate MRI-defined parametrial venous invasion (mrPMVI) for detecting pathological parametrial venous invasion (pPMVI) and its associations with pretreatment lymph node metastasis (LNM) and survival outcomes in locally advanced cervical cancer. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 42 patients with cervical cancer with parametrial invasion on MRI or histopathology, corresponding to International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics 2018 stage IIB or higher disease. Fifteen patients underwent surgery without preoperative therapy and were included in the pathological validation analysis. Image interpretation was primarily based on T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted imaging. Two radiologists independently assessed mrPMVI using a five-point scoring system. Scores ≥ 3 were predefined as mrPMVI-positive. Diagnostic performance for pPMVI and interobserver agreement were evaluated. Univariable logistic and Cox regression analyses were performed for pretreatment LNM and survival outcomes, respectively. RESULTS: pPMVI was present in 10 of 15 patients. The five-point mrPMVI score showed an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.87 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.60-0.98) for detecting pPMVI. The predefined threshold (≥ 3) yielded 30.0% sensitivity and 100% specificity. Interobserver agreement for the five-point mrPMVI score was substantial (linearly weighted κ = 0.75). mrPMVI positivity was associated with pretreatment LNM (odds ratio = 4.00, 95% CI: 1.05-15.26, p = 0.042). During a median follow-up of 24.0 months, 16 patients experienced disease progression and 10 died. mrPMVI positivity was associated with shorter progression-free survival (hazard ratio = 34.25, 95% CI: 4.35-269.91; p < 0.001) and overall survival (hazard ratio = 10.16; 95% CI: 1.28-80.61, p = 0.028). CONCLUSION: The mrPMVI score showed potential for identifying pPMVI, although the predefined threshold was highly specific but insensitive. mrPMVI positivity was associated with pretreatment LNM and survival outcomes, suggesting potential complementary value for risk characterization in locally advanced cervical cancer.

articles.title: An Accountable Encounter-Based Imaging Workflow for Point-of-Care Ultrasound: Integrating Image Availability, Clinician Attribution, and Documentation Accountability.
articles.abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is integral to emergency department (ED) care, but traditional order-based imaging workflows (OBIWs) are poorly aligned with unscheduled encounters and dynamic bedside imaging needs. We describe an accountable encounter-based imaging workflow (EBIW) that integrates patient identification, clinician attribution, encounter-linked image routing, and documentation accountability into a unified imaging informatics architecture. We performed a retrospective observational analysis of aggregated ED POCUS charge data from January 2018 through December 2025 at a single urban academic ED. Three sequential workflows were evaluated: a legacy electronic health record (EHR)-based OBIW, a POCUS Manager-based OBIW, and an accountable EBIW. The accountable EBIW links ultrasound images directly to the ED encounter using barcode-based patient and clinician identification and a centralized Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) router that generates an image availability message. This enables immediate image access in the picture archiving and communication system, EHR, and POCUS management platform before report completion. Charges were not used as a measure of reimbursement or financial return. Because a charge could only be generated after image archival, encounter linkage, documentation, and clinician attestation, charge capture served as a longitudinal system-level marker of completed workflow execution. Charges were normalized by ED visit volume and analyzed using interrupted time series analysis. Transition from the EHR-based OBIW to the POCUS Manager-based OBIW was not associated with an immediate increase in charges. Implementation of the accountable EBIW was associated with an immediate level increase of $11,746 per 1000 visits and a sustained positive quarterly slope thereafter. An accountable EBIW integrating encounter-level acquisition, DICOM routing, immediate image availability, clinician attribution, and documentation accountability was associated with improved capture of ED POCUS utilization.

articles.title: Investigation on Automatic Classification of Bone, Lymph Node, and Local Lesions in CT Images of Prostate Cancer Patients.
articles.abstract: Accurate assessment of different types of prostate cancer (PCa) lesions is a crucial part of treatment planning. Following a computed tomography (CT) or a positron emission tomography (PET)/CT imaging scan, a significant amount of time is required from the clinicians to detect lesions and characterize them by their anatomical locations. To facilitate the development of new image analysis applications, we investigated the potential of automated classification of PCa lesions between bone metastases, lymph node metastases, local lesions, and other PCa lesions in CT images via machine learning (ML) and deep learning models. We annotated a total of 4949 PCa lesions by their type in a private dataset of   18  F-prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT images of 532 PCa patients and an external test set of publicly available PSMA PET/CT images from 30 patients. Using information of coordinates of the detected lesions, we automatically extracted 15 different features from the CT and the results of the automated 3D anatomical segmentation tool TotalSegmentator for each lesion, and trained several traditional ML models to classify lesions by their anatomical type. Additionally, we experimented with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) of different dimensionalities with CT and TotalSegmentator inputs. According to our results, the most accurate model was XGBoost with an overall accuracy of 96.0%. It identified bone metastases, lymph node metastases, and local lesions with sensitivities of 97.9±1.2%, 95.2±1.3%, and 93.1±2.8% in the five-fold cross-validation experiments of the primary data and 96.3%, 94.0%, and 80.0% on the external test set, respectively. Conversely, the CNNs underperformed the best ML models in distinguishing local lesions. To conclude, a simple ML model can accurately classify PCa lesions between bone, lymph node, and local lesions based on CT images, lesion locations, and automated anatomical segmentation data, but more research is required for distinguishing PCa lesions outside these categories.

articles.title: Evaluating Explicit Anatomical Priors Beyond a Mature CT Detector for Six Acute Abdominal Emergencies.
articles.abstract: To test whether anatomical priors from a general-purpose organ segmentation model (TotalSegmentator, TS), applied at inference or during training, improve an externally validated YOLOv11 detector for six acute abdominal emergencies. The frozen detector was applied to 827 external Stanford Merlin CT studies with language-model report labels; a nested 280-study radiologist-adjudicated subset was the reference standard. TS-derived slice selection (Arm A), organ-state integration (Arm B), and their combination (Arm C) were compared with the detector alone under frozen, recalibrated, and fine-tuned conditions. The detector was also retrained from scratch (identical 10-epoch budget) with image channels only, with the patient's TS organ maps as added input channels, or with another patient's maps. AUROC was primary; comparisons used a paired study-level bootstrap. The detector generalized externally (macro AUROC 0.816 cohort; 0.879 adjudicated). Slice selection was non-inferior but not beneficial: nearly all confident detections already lay within the anchored organ's axial range; organ-state fusion improved AUROC only for cholecystitis (hypothesis-generating). In single runs, training with organ maps raised internal test mAP@0.5 (0.517 versus 0.482), and the model depended on the maps, but external macro AUROC did not improve (0.822 versus 0.829; Δ -0.007, 95% CI -0.019 to +0.007) and kidney-stone AUROC fell (0.678 versus 0.768; exploratory), unlike with another patient's maps. Per-site recalibration was the most effective operating-point adjustment (macro F1 +0.021); annotation-free fine-tuning reduced discrimination. Explicit anatomy, applied after detection or during training, did not improve this detector's overall external discrimination. Per-site recalibration gave the largest operating-point gain.

articles.title: Diagnosis of Suspected Pituitary Microadenomas: The Complementary Role of Habitat-based Non-enhanced MRI Radiomics Features.
articles.abstract: To develop and validate a combined model for detecting pituitary microadenomas in suspected cases using non-contrast T1-weighted sagittal (T1SAG) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and to assess its performance as a non-contrast imaging-based tool for clinical decision support.This retrospective two-center study enrolled 519 patients with suspected pituitary microadenomas, divided into a training set (n = 321), an internal validation set (n = 80), and an external test set (n = 118). Radiomics features were extracted from both the entire pituitary gland and its habitat subregions, generated via unsupervised K-means clustering. Eight predictive models were constructed using logistic regression: a clinical model, an intra-pituitary radiomics model, three individual habitat models (Habitat 1, 2, and 3), an early-fusion model combining all habitats, an ensemble model integrating the probability outputs of the three habitat models, and a combined model that integrated clinical, intra-pituitary, and the optimal fusion model. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves (ROC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.Among all models, the combined model demonstrated the best predictive performance across all three cohorts, achieving areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.885 (95% CI: 0.850-0.920) in the training set, 0.788 (95% CI: 0.690-0.885) in the internal validation set, and 0.796 (95% CI: 0.712-0.880) in the external test set. The combined model also achieved the highest accuracy and sensitivity across all datasets.The combined prediction model showed robust performance in distinguishing pituitary microadenomas in suspected cases, offering enhanced clinical decision support while reducing dependence on contrast-enhanced MRI examinations.

articles.title: Building and Validating a Data-Governance Workflow for Artificial Intelligence-Based Tuberculosis Detection from Chest Radiographs, and Quantifying the Impact of Data Leakage.
articles.abstract: Studies applying artificial intelligence (AI) to tuberculosis (TB) detection from chest radiographs (CXR) focus on models and metrics, yet the quality, provenance and reproducibility of the data workflow decide the reliability of results; duplicate images and non-patient-level splitting inflate evaluation metrics. We propose a seven-step data-governance workflow: multi-source standardisation, provenance management, three-hash deduplication (MD5, pHash, dHash), patient-level splitting, invariant-check auditing, lung segmentation and version freezing by data fingerprint. Four leakage scenarios (deduplication on or off; patient-level or random split) were repeated 20 times with paired splits and compared with the clean scenario on per-repeat differences. On 46,410 CXR images from seven public sources, the workflow removed duplicates at file and content level, standardised 16,554 TB Portals DICOM images, generated 34,554 lung masks without failure and sealed every layer with SHA-256 hashes. On the three-class multi-source corpus, the area under the curve (AUC) saturated near 0.997 in every scenario, consistent with source-class confounding; paired leakage effects were statistically detectable but below 0.1 percentage points. On a single-source probe task (drug resistance within TB Portals), random image-level splitting inflated the internal AUC by 1.7 percentage points (95% confidence interval 0.9 to 2.4; p = 0.001), or 1.2 points after a deduplication gap found during revision was repaired; in a holdout design, an internal gap of 1.1 points shrank to 0.4 points on a patient-disjoint holdout. The magnitude of leakage depends on data structure and must be measured; a rigorous governance workflow makes that measurement, and data reuse, verifiable.

articles.title: Ultra-High Gradient Thin-Slice Oblique Coronal Zoomed DWI for Perihilar and Distal Cholangiocarcinomas: Improved Tumor Depiction for Precise Surgical Planning.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Accurate preoperative assessment of extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (eCCA) remains challenging with conventional imaging. This study aimed to investigate the value of thin-slice oblique coronal zoomed diffusion-weighted imaging (OC-Z-DWI) on an ultra-high gradient system for eCCA (including both perihilar and distal subtypes) assessment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 93 patients with pathologically diagnosed eCCA (54 males, 66.8 ± 9.0 years; 62 perihilar and 31 distal) and 43 patients without eCCA (19 males, 62.9 ± 11.8 years). All patients underwent conventional magnetic resonance imaging and OC-Z-DWI on an ultra-high gradient system (200 mT/m amplitude). Image quality of OC-Z-DWI was evaluated, and diagnostic performance and lesion sizing were compared between the conventional protocol and one incorporating OC-Z-DWI. RESULTS: OC-Z-DWI showed good scoring in noise, artifacts, and overall image quality (mean 3.83 ± 0.41, 3.65 ± 0.56, and 3.80 ± 0.43, respectively). Adding OC-Z-DWI to the conventional protocol significantly improved lesion edge sharpness (3.89 ± 0.31 vs 3.60 ± 0.53, P < 0.001), lesion conspicuity (3.94 ± 0.25 vs 3.75 ± 0.46, P < 0.001), diagnostic confidence (3.86 ± 0.38 vs 3.58 ± 0.65, P < 0.001), and diagnostic performance (AUC 0.917 vs 0.869, P = 0.018). Lesion size measurements with the OC-Z-DWI-based protocol demonstrated strong pathological correlation (r = 0.822), with lower pathological-imaging diameter discrepancy than the conventional protocol (median 4.0 mm vs 7.0 mm, P < 0.001). These improvements were consistent across both perihilar and distal subgroups. Furthermore, R0 resection patients exhibited a stronger imaging-pathology sizing correlation than R1 patients (r = 0.891 vs 0.528, P = 0.021). CONCLUSION: Ultra-high gradient thin-slice OC-Z-DWI provides high-quality images for eCCA characterization. Adding OC-Z-DWI to the conventional magnetic resonance protocol enhances lesion delineation, diagnostic performance, and tumor sizing accuracy, delivering more precise preoperative information to optimize surgical planning.

articles.title: Retrospective Lung-RADS v2022 Characterization of Fatal Lung Cancer Cases in the National Lung Screening Trial.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Persistent lung cancer mortality despite screening is multifactorial. Characterizing computed tomography (CT) findings preceding fatal lung cancer may identify imaging features and screening challenges that warrant further study. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, outcome-enriched case series nested within the 26,722-participant low-dose computed tomography arm of the National Lung Screening Trial. Among 359 participants who died of lung cancer within the prespecified interval, exclusions for positive baseline screening (n = 186), incomplete screening (n = 28), withdrawal/declined screening (n = 19), unavailable CTs (n = 6), or three negative screens followed by death 2+ years after the final screen (n = 29) yielded 91 participants. Screening CTs were retrospectively assessed using the Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) v2022. Four thoracic radiologists independently reviewed visible-in-retrospect nodules and adjudicated whether they met criteria for suspicion. RESULTS: Of 91 participants, 22 (24%; 95% confidence interval (CI), 17%-34%) had visible-in-retrospect nodules considered suspicious under Lung-RADS v2022 ("missed"), 16 (18%; 95% CI, 11%-27%) had visible nodules not meeting suspicion criteria ("not callable"), 50 (55%; 95% CI, 45%-65%) had no visible-in-retrospect nodule, and 3 (3.3%) were inconclusive. Missed nodules were frequently juxtapleural (41%), obscured (50%), or irregularly bordered (68%); not-callable nodules were frequently <6 mm (75%), juxtapleural (56%), or irregularly bordered (56%). CONCLUSION: In this selected fatal-case series, small and juxtapleural nodules were common among visible nodules not meeting Lung-RADS v2022 suspicion criteria. These findings warrant evaluation in representative screening populations and should not be interpreted as estimates of population-level Lung-RADS performance.

articles.title: Decoding Spatial Attention in the Cocktail Party Problem Using Whole-head High-Density fNIRS.
articles.abstract: Spatial attention is critical for solving the cocktail party problem, a longstanding problem in neuroscience and artificial speech recognition. The ability to decode where humans are attending in a cocktail party like scene would empower applications in brain computer interfaces and assistive devices such as hearing aids. Here we demonstrate that, in an overt attention task, the attended spatial location can be decoded robustly from single trial hemodynamic responses, using a whole head high density fNIRS system. We also identify critical brain regions that make the highest contribution to decoding accuracy. Specifically, we find that decoding based on a small fraction of channels located within the left and right inferior parietal lobule (IPL) achieves maximal decoding accuracy comparable to all channels. Decoding fell close to chance in a covert auditory condition in which participants held central fixation while attending to the same talkers, indicating that auditory attention alone without orientation is not sufficient for decoding. Finally, control experiments suggest that overt-condition decoding is influenced by sustained eye position/gaze direction, not eye movement. These results support the development of fNIRS-integrated BCIs and assistive devices controlled by overt spatial attention.

articles.title: Celiac Plexus Neurolysis Combined with Intratumoral Injection Improves Pain Control Compared with Neurolysis Alone in Patients with Cancer-Related Upper Abdominal Pain Due to Celiac Plexus Invasion: A Retrospective Study.
Physics-constrained and geometry-aware deep reconstruction for limited-angle CBCT.
articles.abstract: Limited-angle cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is attractive for imageguided radiotherapy and imaging-guided procedure when full-arc acquisition is impractical, but the incomplete angular sampling leads to severe streaking, shading, and structural distortion. This study aimed to develop a physics-constrained and geometry-aware deep reconstruction framework for recovering anatomically faithful volumetric CBCT from limited-angle projections.Approach: We propose PCGA-Net, a dual-domain reconstruction framework that combines projection completion, analytic geometric reconstruction, and image-domain refinement within a unified cross-domain design. Specifically, a projection completion module first estimates missingangle information from the measured limited-angle projections. A geometry-aware reconstruction module then maps the completed projections into image space using differentiable cone-beam forward and backward-projection operators. Finally, a volumetric refinement module suppresses residual artifacts and restores anatomical detail under geometry-guided cross-domain consistency supervision. The framework was evaluated on three cohorts: gynecologic highdose-rate brachytherapy, abdominal liver 4DCT, and head-and-neck CBCT.Main Results: Across all three cohorts, PCGA-Net consistently outperformed conventional limitedangle FDK reconstruction and the compared learning-based baselines, cGAN and PatRecon-Net, in both qualitative and quantitative evaluation. On the gynecologic HDR brachytherapy cohort, PCGA-Net achieved an MAE of 34.47 ± 6.28 HU, an SSIM of 0.87 ± 0.04, and a PSNR of 35.79 ± 0.95 dB. On the abdominal liver 4DCT cohort, PCGA-Net achieved 39.27 ± 6.10 HU MAE, 0.82 ± 0.03 SSIM, and 36.85 ± 1.16 dB PSNR.On the head-and-neck CBCT cohort, PCGA-Net achieved 28.42 ± 4.88 HU MAE, 0.91 ± 0.05 SSIM, and 38.52 ± 0.95 dB PSNR. In all three cohorts, PCGA-Net exceeded cGAN and PatRecon-Net across all evaluated metrics. Significance: These results indicate that jointly enforcing projection-domain completion, analytic imaging geometry, and image-domain refinement is an effective strategy for limited-angle CBCT reconstruction. PCGA-Net provides a robust short-arc reconstruction framework across multiple anatomical sites, supporting its potential utility in constrained imageguided therapeutic and procedural settings.

articles.title: Physics-informed neural network for photoacoustic tomography reconstruction.
articles.abstract: Conventional photoacoustic tomography (PAT) reconstruction algorithms often suffer from performance degradation under complex media and non-ideal detection conditions. To tackle these limitations, we propose a novel reconstruction method based on physics-informed neural networks (PINNs).Approach:The network model is optimized with constraints from observational data, wave equation, and initial conditions, to reconstruct the spatial distribution of initial acoustic pressure. The PINN framework further incorporates time reversal method to improve computational efficiency.Main results:Comprehensive PAT simulations demonstrate that the PINN achieves superior reconstruction quality compared with conventional algorithms. The PINN exhibits favorable adaptivity to both heterogeneous and lossy media, and strong robustness against noisy measurements, sparse sensor layouts and limited-view detection geometries.Significance:The PINN integrates the physical interpretability and the powerful capability of neural networks to represent continuous acoustic pressure fields. It eliminates the requirement for training datasets, offering broad application potential for PAT.

articles.title: Physics-informed machine learning-based dose calculation for patients undergoing fluoroscopically guided interventional procedures.
articles.abstract: To develop and evaluate a physics-informed machine-learning framework for rapid organ-dose estimation in fluoroscopically guided interventional procedures without requiring patient-specific imaging.Approach: We used 385 adult radiation dose structured reports from three procedure types-bilateral carotid angiography, percutaneous biliary drainage, and liver chemoembolization-comprising more than 50,000 irradiation events. A body-size-matched computational phantom was selected using patient sex, height, and weight. RDSR-derived beam parameters and engineered descriptors of beam-organ geometry and attenuation were used to train organ-specific XGBoost models for localized organs and a multi-output multilayer perceptron model for four distributed tissues. Monte Carlo-derived dose coefficients from NCIRF3 were used as target values.Main results: In the held-out test set of 12,683 irradiation events, 49.4% and 84.8% of XGBoost-based localized-organ estimates were within ±5% and ±20% of the Monte Carlo-derived values, respectively. The corresponding proportions were 88.2% and 98.0% for the distributed-tissue estimates and 87.6% and 98.3% for detriment-weighted dose. The median relative prediction error across organs and tissues was 0.37% (interquartile range, -3.68% to 4.99%). A reliability score was developed to support uncertainty-aware interpretation. The framework required approximately 0.3 s per irradiation event, corresponding to an approximately 290-fold acceleration relative to conventional Monte Carlo simulation under the benchmark conditions.Significance: The proposed image-free framework enables rapid organ-dose estimation when patient imaging is unavailable and may support large retrospective epidemiological studies and uncertainty-aware dose monitoring. Because development and validation were limited to three procedure types and relied on reconstructed phantom-beam geometry, external validation is required before application to other procedures or high-precision individual clinical decisions.

articles.title: Adaptive physics-inspired angular-spatial modeling for multi-shell diffusion MRI denoising.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Multi-shell diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) provides rich q-space information but is susceptible to noise, which can disrupt spatial anatomy, intra-shell directional relationships, inter-shell signal attenuation, and downstream diffusion parameter estimation. We aim to develop a denoising method that jointly preserves spatial structure, directional information, and shell-specific signal characteristics. APPROACH: We propose ASD-NCSM, an adaptive physics-inspired angular-spatial framework with a fixed three-stage alternating architecture. It combines intra-shell differential angular graph message passing with 2.5D spatial residual refinement. Noise-Conditioned Shell Modulation (NCSM) adaptively regulates angular updates according to b-value, spatial residual and angular dispersion proxies, and local gating. A Shell-wise Physical Attenuation and Angular Relation Consistency (SPARC) objective further constrains shell-wise signal fidelity, logarithmic attenuation, and local angular structure. The model was evaluated on HCP multi-shell dMRI with simulated noise and independently acquired real in vivo brain dMRI data. MAIN RESULTS: Across five simulated noise levels from 2% to 10%, ASD-NCSM achieved the best overall DWI restoration among MPPCA, 1D-CNN, ECDM, SAN2N, and dMRI-Swin, with consistent subject-level advantages in PSNR, SSIM, and NRMSE. At 6% noise, principal-direction angular nRMSE was 32.68 ± 2.76%, with significant differences from all five baselines after Holm correction. ASD-NCSM also achieved the lowest mean MAE for FA, MD, AD, and RD, and the lowest relative MAE for ODI and FISO, while NDI was comparable to 1D-CNN and dMRI-Swin. For real data without noise-free references, Q-PEFT yielded the lowest angular cross-fit inconsistency (2.29 ± 0.10%) across three test subjects while maintaining limited signal and downstream-parameter changes. SIGNIFICANCE: ASD-NCSM jointly preserves spatial continuity, directional geometry, and shell-level attenuation, providing balanced signal recovery, directional preservation, and downstream parameter stability for multi-shell dMRI denoising.

articles.title: High-fidelity 3D geometric reconstruction of pelvic organs from MRI: a hybrid deep learning and iterative optimization approach.
articles.abstract: The generation of high-fidelity, high-quality three-dimensional (3D) pelvic organ geometries from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived segmentation masks remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a hybrid framework for reconstructing the bladder, uterus, and rectum, and to assess its geometric fidelity, mesh-quality proxy performance, and reconstruction efficiency.Approach. We developed a hybrid deformable shape modeling framework that integrates deep learning prediction with iterative optimization for the reconstruction of the bladder, uterus, and rectum. The framework consists of three core components: (1) a geometry-aware multi-level deep learning architecture that preserves topological consistency of pelvic organs; (2) a two-stage amortized optimization training strategy that balances global shape capture and local surface refinement; and (3) a holistic synergy mechanism-where iterative optimization provides supervision for deep learning during the training phase, and during inference, deep learning rapidly predicts the global organ morphology, followed by iterative optimization to refine local surfaces and mesh quality.Main results. Before iterative refinement, the proposed model outperformed representative deep learning-based reconstruction methods in geometric fidelity, achieving CD/DSC values of 5.5 × 10⁻³/0.788 for the bladder, 3.7 × 10⁻³/0.839 for the rectum, and 4.2 × 10⁻³/0.900 for the uterus. Deep learning-based initialization enabled the complete hybrid framework to converge within approximately 100 iterations, with a reconstruction time of approximately 35 s per organ on a CPU and 1.5 s on a GPU. At the patient level, the mean minSICN and minSIGE values of the 10 worst volumetric elements were 0.0807 and 0.0844, respectively, exceeding those achieved by traditional geometric post-processing methods.Significance. The proposed framework connects image-domain segmentation with structural-domain applications by efficiently generating high-fidelity, high-quality pelvic organ geometries with improved mesh-quality proxy performance. These geometries may support statistical shape assessment and may provide candidate surface representations for subsequent volumetric meshing and solver-specific biomechanical validation.

articles.title: Pulmonary embolism in pregnancy and the postpartum period: 16-Year trends in CT pulmonary angiography and lung scintigraphy.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate 16-year trends in utilisation, radiation exposure, and diagnostic yield of computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) and lung scintigraphy (LS) for suspected pulmonary embolism (PE) during pregnancy and postpartum period. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Pregnant and ≤ 6-week postpartum patients undergoing CTPA or LS from 2008 to 2024 were retrospectively studied. CTPA maternal effective, breast absorbed and modelled foetal effective doses were estimated using Monte Carlo modelling. LS maternal effective, breast absorbed and foetal absorbed doses were calculated from administered activity using ICRP coefficients. RESULTS: Of 1,140 imaging examinations, 945 occurred during pregnancy (619 LS; 326 CTPA) and 195 postpartum (33 LS; 162 CTPA). LS comprised 65.5% of pregnancy examinations but 16.9% postpartum compared with 34.5% and 83.1% for CTPA respectively (p < 0.001). CTPA use increased while LS use declined. During pregnancy, PE was detected in 16/619 LS examinations (2.6%) and 12/326 CTPAs (3.7%); postpartum, in 0/33 LS examinations and 11/162 CTPAs (6.8%). Median maternal effective doses during pregnancy were 0.544 mSv for LS (IQR 0.512-0.593, n = 449) and 2.96 mSv for CTPA (IQR 2.23-3.74, n = 305); postpartum effective doses were 1.126 mSv (IQR1.045-1.243, n = 10) and 1.69 mSv (IQR 1.43-2.42, n = 142), respectively. Breast absorbed dose was higher with CTPA during pregnancy and postpartum (both p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Over 16 years, imaging shifted from LS towards CTPA. Diagnostic yield remained low, as expected in a rule-out population, while CTPA was associated with higher maternal effective and breast absorbed doses than LS. These findings underscore the importance of appropriate imaging selection in this population.

articles.title: Deep learning super-resolution enhances MRI radiomics for predicting placenta accreta spectrum and invasiveness.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) is a severe obstetric complication. This study evaluated whether retrospective, post-processing deep learning-based super-resolution reconstruction (SR) was associated with improved MRI radiomics performance for predicting PAS and invasive PAS. MATERIALS & METHODS: This retrospective study involved 245 patients who had placental MRI scans at three different institutions. Of these, 158 cases from Institution I for training set and internal validation set, while 34 patients from Institution II and 53 patients from Institution III served as external validation sets. SR using a generative adversarial network (GAN) was applied to generate SR T2WI (SRT2WI). Predictive models for PAS and invasive PAS were developed based on T2WI, SRT2WI, and the SRT2WI-Clinical model. Two radiologists independently diagnosed PAS using T2WI to serve as a reference for evaluating model performance. Model performance was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), Delong test, and net reclassification improvement (NRI). SHAP values interpreted the models and quantified feature contributions. RESULTS: Across all four cohorts, SRT2WI yielded numerically higher AUCs than T2WI, and SRT2WI-Clinical achieved the highest AUCs. For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical achieved AUCs of 0.953, 0.887, 0.793, and 0.788 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts 1 and 2, respectively (T2WI: 0.738, 0.697, 0.654, and 0.652; SRT2WI: 0.879, 0.820, 0.696, and 0.768). Corresponding AUCs for invasive PAS were 0.895, 0.875, 0.843, and 0.815 (T2WI: 0.774, 0.699, 0.575, and 0.745; SRT2WI: 0.861, 0.794, 0.729, and 0.808). For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical significantly outperformed T2WI (P < 0.001) and SRT2WI (P = 0.004) only in training, with no significant validation differences. For invasive PAS, it significantly outperformed T2WI in training, internal validation, and external validation cohort 1 (P = 0.003, 0.021, and 0.019, respectively), but not external validation cohort 2 (P = 0.398); comparisons with SRT2WI were nonsignificant. Calibration showed good agreement, DCA favored SRT2WI-Clinical, and SHAP quantified feature contributions. CONCLUSIONS: The combination of SR and radiomics shows promise for improving the prediction of PAS and invasive PAS. Integrating clinical features may further enhance model performance, supporting its potential clinical utility.

articles.title: Large language model assistance for report-based carotid plaque AHA classification: a multi-reader study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether large language model assistance improves radiologists' agreement with a text-based reference standard in inferring the modified American Heart Association carotid plaque classification from free-text MRI reports, and whether a lightweight model can perform well under criteria-guided prompting. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 433 patients from three institutions. In a report-based reader study, four radiologists classified MRI reports with and without large language model assistance. In standalone evaluation, a rule-based baseline and 10 models were compared under naive and criteria-guided prompting. The reference standard was expert consensus based on the report text. RESULTS: Among 433 patients (mean age, 65.9 years ± 13.4; 248 males), AI assistance improved six-class agreement with the text-based reference standard. At the vessel level, junior radiologists improved from 61.75% to 83.12% (Qwen3-8B) and 87.75% (DeepSeek-R1); senior radiologists from 77.00% to 87.50% and 92.25%, respectively (all Holm-corrected p < 0.001). Patient-level agreement increased from 41.0% to 78.8% (junior) and from 59.8% to 87.8% (senior) with DeepSeek-R1. Agreement increased (quadratic-weighted κ: 0.231 without AI vs 0.775 with DeepSeek-R1). In standalone evaluation, criteria-guided prompting improved Qwen3-8B agreement from 38.91% to 81.52% (95% CI: 78.87-84.06%), remaining 5.89 percentage points below DeepSeek-R1 (87.41%; 95% CI: 85.10-89.61%). CONCLUSION: In this report-based classification setting, large language model assistance improved radiologists' agreement with the text-based reference standard, with larger gains in junior radiologists. When prompts explicitly encoded AHA criteria, an 8B local candidate model performed well, supporting its potential use as a standardization aid for text-based workflows. KEY POINTS: Question Report-based modified AHA classification of carotid plaques is experience-dependent and difficult to standardize, as mapping multi-sequence imaging findings to classification conclusions imposes substantial cognitive load. Findings Large language model assistance improved agreement with a text-based reference standard and raised inter-reader consistency (weighted κ 0.231-0.775), narrowing the junior-senior gap. Critical relevance statement Embedding explicit AHA criteria in the prompt let an 8B model approach 671B-model agreement (38.91-81.52%), supporting standardized text-based workflows without fine-tuning.

articles.title: The underestimated risk of additional ipsilateral BI-RADS 3 lesions identified by preoperative ultrasound in breast cancer patients.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of malignancy of additional ultrasound BI-RADS category 3 lesions in women with newly diagnosed breast cancer. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Between July 2014 and June 2022, women with newly diagnosed breast cancer and additional ultrasound BI-RADS 3 lesions were retrospectively included. Malignancy was confirmed by pathology, and malignancy rates were assessed at both the patient and lesion levels. Independent risk factors for malignant BI-RADS 3 lesions were identified using multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: A total of 1458 women (median age, 45 years; IQR: 40-51) with 1995 ultrasound BI-RADS 3 lesions were included. At the patient level, malignancy was identified in 3.5% of patients (51/1458), with higher rates for ipsilateral than contralateral BI-RADS 3 lesions (9.8% [39/397] vs 1.1% [12/1061]; p < 0.001). At the lesion level, the overall malignancy rate was 2.7% (54/1995), similarly elevated for ipsilateral compared with contralateral lesions (7.5% [41/544] vs 0.9% [13/1451]; p < 0.001). Independent predictors for malignancy of ipsilateral BI-RADS 3 lesions included same-quadrant location as the primary lesion (OR, 4.3; 95% CI: 1.9, 9.7; p < 0.001), ultrasonographic architectural distortion of the primary lesion (OR, 8.5; 95% CI: 1.6, 46.1; p = 0.01), and mammographic suspicious calcification of the primary lesion (OR, 2.9; 95% CI: 1.4, 6.0; p = 0.004). CONCLUSION: Additional ipsilateral ultrasound BI-RADS 3 lesions in women with newly diagnosed breast cancer demonstrated malignancy rates exceeding the 2% BI-RADS threshold, particularly when located in the same quadrant as the primary cancer. KEY POINTS: Question The malignancy risk of additional BI-RADS 3 lesions identified by preoperative ultrasound in breast cancer patients remains unclear. Findings Ipsilateral lesions, especially in the same quadrant, show malignancy rates exceeding 2%, while malignancy risk remains low for contralateral BI-RADS 3 lesions. Critical relevance statement Ipsilateral BI-RADS 3 lesions in the same quadrant as the primary cancer, or those with primary tumor architectural distortion or suspicious calcifications, warrant biopsy. This ensures precise surgical planning and avoids missing additional malignancy.

articles.title: Automated Segmentation of Wound Bed Tissue from Clinical Photographs: A Benchmark of Five Deep Learning Architectures Under a Shared Protocol.
articles.abstract: Accurate characterisation of the wound bed, the relative proportions of granulation, slough and necrotic tissue described by the red-yellow-black model, is central to monitoring healing and guiding debridement in chronic-wound care, yet in routine practice, it is judged visually and is poorly reproducible between clinicians. We investigated automatic, pixel-level segmentation of these three classes within the wound region of interest. A corpus of 404 photographs was curated from a public wound image collection and densely annotated by wound care clinicians with a purpose-built, cluster-assisted labelling tool. Five deep learning architectures spanning convolutional, transformer, hybrid and ensemble families were trained on one frozen data split under a largely shared pipeline, with limited, fully documented architecture-specific tuning, and scored on a shared 62-image test set. The models fell within a narrow mean intersection-over-union band (0.748-0.818). The strongest single model, a purely convolutional network, was statistically indistinguishable from the best ensemble, and simply averaging already-trained convolutional and transformer models matched that ensemble at no additional training cost. Slough remained consistently the hardest tissue. Translated into clinical units, per-wound tissue percentages were recovered with small mean bias (within ± 5 percentage points) but wide single-image limits of agreement (about ± 25-50 percentage points), so the measurement suits aggregate and longitudinal assessment rather than single-image reading. Within this dataset, split and training protocol, the choice among the strong hierarchical architectures was not decisive: a single strong model is the pragmatic option for clinical deployment, with an ensemble reserved for maximal accuracy and class balance.

articles.title: Patient acceptance and experience with contrast-enhanced mammography in women with a personal history of breast cancer: findings from the COMBO trial.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate patient acceptance, tolerability and experience with contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM) in women with a personal history of breast cancer undergoing routine post-surgical surveillance. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective cohort study, conducted within the COMBO Trial, included consecutive women with a personal history of breast cancer undergoing CEM instead of digital mammography (DM) for routine surveillance from January 2023 to February 2025. Immediately after the examination, participants completed an anonymous 16-question questionnaire assessing discomfort, pain, exam duration, pre-examination reassurance, information received, anxiety, contrast injection, satisfaction and comparative experience with prior DM. Responses used Likert-type scales. Descriptive and non-parametric analyses were performed (p < 0.05 statistically significant). RESULTS: Of 969 eligible women, 936 (mean age 58.2 years, SD ± 10.2 years) completed the questionnaire. CEM was perceived as comparable to prior DM in terms of discomfort (631/936; 67.4%), pain (725/936; 77.4%), positioning (717/936; 76.6%) and duration (601/936; 64.3%). Overall satisfaction was high (900/936; 96.2%), and 932/936 (99.6%) of participants would recommend CEM. Although 433/936 (46.3%) of women reported moderate-to-high pre-examination anxiety, higher anxiety was significantly associated with greater perceived discomfort, pain, uncomfortable positioning, longer examination duration, lower reassurance, lower comfort during contrast medium administration, and lower overall satisfaction (all p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In this large cohort of breast cancer survivors, CEM demonstrated high acceptance, satisfaction and tolerability in post-surgical follow-up. Although pre-examination anxiety negatively influenced examination experience, it did not reduce patients' willingness to undergo CEM, supporting its integration into personalised post-treatment breast cancer surveillance. KEY POINTS: Question Evidence on patient acceptance and tolerability of CEM for routine post-surgical surveillance in women with previous breast cancer is limited. Findings In 936 breast cancer survivors, CEM showed high satisfaction and tolerability, while pre-examination anxiety was associated with a less favourable experience. Critical Relevance Statement High patient acceptance supports CEM as a feasible surveillance option after breast cancer treatment, while the association between anxiety and poorer experience highlights the radiologist's role in pre-examination communication and reassurance.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of a modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop a modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system and validate its diagnostic performance. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system was developed by incorporating the significant signs from the standard O-RADS MRI system. This study retrospectively enrolled the 176 adnexal masses in cohort A. MRI imaging features were compared between benign and malignant tumors within this cohort. The diagnostic performance of the two scoring models was assessed by estimating the area under the curve (AUC), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). In addition, 352 adnexal lesions from cohorts B and C were included to further evaluate the diagnostic ability of the modified scoring system. RESULTS: In cohort A, the papillary projections exhibiting the sea anemone sign were highly indicative of borderline lesions (p = 0.001). Diffusion restriction in solid components significantly distinguished benign from malignant masses (p = 0.001). The apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) value of cystic components yielded a cutoff of 1.74 (p < 0.05). The DeLong test revealed no statistically significant difference in AUCs between the two systems in cohort A (p > 0.05). The NRI and IDI for the modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system were -4.13% and -0.04, respectively (all p > 0.05). In cohorts B and C, the AUCs were 0.933 and 0.910. CONCLUSION: The diagnostic efficacy of the modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system was comparable to that of the standard O-RADS MRI risk stratification system, facilitating the distinction between benign and malignant adnexal neoplasms. KEY POINTS: Question How can a modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system be developed, and can this scoring system accurately classify adnexal masses? Findings The modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI system demonstrates excellent diagnostic performance and reliable risk stratification of adnexal masses by evaluating key imaging features. Critical relevance statement The modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system contributes to the risk stratification of adnexal masses, particularly for patients who cannot undergo contrast agent administration. This system provides a reliable tool to optimize treatment strategies and improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Risk-adapted MRI Protocols for the Detection of Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer.
articles.abstract: Purpose To compare the diagnostic performance and clinical utility of three MRI protocols for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) according to prebiopsy risk. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included 390 male patients who underwent prostate multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) between January 2019 and April 2024 for suspected csPCa, followed by biopsy. Patients were stratified by Rotterdam Prostate Cancer Risk Calculator score into low-risk (<4%), intermediate-risk (4%-9%), and high-risk (≥10%) groups. Three datasets were generated from each examination: mpMRI (T2-weighted imaging, diffusion-weighted imaging [DWI], and dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging), unenhanced MRI (multiplanar T2-weighted imaging and DWI), and short MRI (axial T2-weighted imaging and DWI). Overall, 1170 datasets were randomly assigned to 10 expert radiologists (117 examinations each). Diagnostic performance for grade group 2 or greater cancer and clinical utility metrics were compared across risk groups. Results Among the 390 patients (median age, 66 years [IQR, 61-71 years]), csPCa prevalence was 34.4% (134 of 390). In low-risk patients, short MRI demonstrated the highest sensitivity (95% [21 of 22]), with no significant differences among protocols (all P ≥ .21) and greatest potential for safe biopsy avoidance (84 biopsies avoided per missed csPCa). In intermediate-risk patients, mpMRI showed higher sensitivity (83% vs 72% for unenhanced MRI and 62% for short MRI; P = .012 for mpMRI vs short MRI) and higher biopsy efficiency (1.11 vs 0.85 for mpMRI vs unenhanced MRI). In high-risk patients, protocol-related differences were minimal (all P ≥ .12). Conclusion mpMRI was associated with improved sensitivity and biopsy efficiency in intermediate-risk patients, whereas protocol differences were limited in low- and high-risk groups; these findings support risk-adapted selection of MRI protocols. Keywords: MR-Dynamic Contrast-enhanced, MR Imaging, Urinary, Prostate, Neoplasms-Primary, Efficacy Studies, Prostatic Neoplasms, MRI, Contrast Medium, Biopsy, Risk Assessment Supplemental material is available for this article. © RSNA, 2026.

articles.title: Direct probabilistic IMPT treatment planning with setup and range errors for neuro-oncological patients.
articles.abstract: Objective. To show computational feasibility of a previously proposed probabilistic planning approach on a neuro-oncological patient group, we compared probabilistic plans with (automated) robust plans for one patient (group A) that could achieve sufficient clinical target coverage and for four patients (group B) where target coverage had to be compromised due to organ-at-risk (OAR) dose constraints.Approach. The probabilistic approach is percentile-based and uses the fact that a (dose) percentile can be approximated as a linear combination of its expected value and standard deviation. This allows us to formulate objectives and constraints with patient-specific acceptance probabilities. The optimization has a nested structure: the inner optimization optimizes the beam weights for a given percentile estimate, while an outer loop iteratively updates and improves the accuracy of the percentile estimate. For every outer iteration, the optimization is warm-started from the previous iteration. Percentiles are efficiently calculated by sampling a polynomial chaos expansion of the dose-influence matrix.Main results. The patient in group A achieved cumulative OAR dose reductions (of OAR-related DVH-metrics) of 23.1 GyRBE, for identical target coverage. Target coverage improved for all patients in group B (the 10th percentile ofincreased up to 0.61 GyRBE), at the same time reaching cumulative OAR dose reductions (of OAR-related DVH-metrics) up to about 40 GyRBE. Probabilistic plans were optimized in 44 h to 226 h. For two representative patients, eliminating warm-starting (i.e. the outer loop) from the approach reduced total optimization times to below 10 h (which took originally 80 h and 141 h).Significance. Compared to robust optimization methods, the probabilistic approach achieves improved trade-offs between probabilistic target coverage and OAR sparing, potentially leading to better treatments.

articles.title: Integrating Histotripsy into Chemoimmunotherapy for Oligometastatic Recurrent Extrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma: Case Report.
articles.abstract: The management of advanced, recurrent extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma has shifted toward prolonged systemic therapy including immune checkpoint inhibition. Incorporating local treatment for oligometastatic or oligoprogressive disease without interrupting systemic therapy remains challenging. Conventional liver-directed therapies frequently require a chemotherapy break. Histotripsy is a noninvasive, non-thermal, non-ionizing modality that permits continuation of systemic therapy. This case presents a 71-year-old woman with recurrent extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma who developed multifocal hepatic metastases while receiving gemcitabine and durvalumab.
